description:
Filed s396 while implementing #325 (refaliasing).  The ASSIGNMENT forms all
work now; this is the FOREACH spelling, and its blocker is PPI, not the alias.

THE SHAPES (both measured, both currently TRANSPILE-FAIL):
  t/op/const-optree.t   148 rows   `for \%_ (@tests) {...}`     (package hash)
  t/op/lvref.t          ~8 rows    `for \my $topic (...)`, `for \my @a (...)`,
                                   `for \my %a (...)`, `for \$::a(...)`,
                                   `for \@::a(...)`, `for \%::a(...)`,
                                   `for \&a(...)`   (op/lvref.t also needs #314
                                   family F-F first -- `\state @a = [1..3]`)

WHY IT DIES: PPI only lexes `foreach [my] $scalar (LIST) BLOCK`.  Both the
`\`-cast and a non-scalar loop variable break it, and the damage is not local:
the Statement::Compound comes out holding ONLY the word `for`, and the rest of
the construct AND EVERY FOLLOWING STATEMENT are swallowed into one flat
PPI::Statement sibling.  Verified by dumping the tree.  The die you see is
`Parser2 TODO: foreach without list` (Parser2.pm ~7205) -- accurate, since the
compound really has no list child.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX (the s395/#270 pattern -- repair the RAW TOKEN STREAM,
then reparse; do NOT try tree surgery, the enclosing structure is unfinished):
walk the token stream for Word(for|foreach) + Cast(\) + [Word(my|our|state)] +
Symbol + `(`, and rewrite the run into a shape PPI DOES lex, prepending the
alias to the block body so the mechanism #325 already shipped does the work:

    for \my %e (@list) { BODY }
      =>  for my $__PCL_RA0 (@list) { \my %e = $__PCL_RA0; BODY }

That is a pure re-spelling: `\my %e = $tmp` is an ordinary declaration plus
the p-setf \-cast place, so no new foreach macro, no VarAnnotator work, and %e
is scoped to the body and fresh per iteration -- exactly perl.  Edit token
CONTENT only (set_content on the Cast -> `my`, on the Symbol -> the temp name,
append the alias statement to the `{` token) and call _reparse_doc, exactly as
_repair_swallowing_prototypes does.

THE ONE SEMANTIC QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST (probe it, do not assume): perl
implicitly LOCALIZES a PACKAGE loop variable, so after `for \%::a (...)` the
package hash is restored -- the naive rewrite above leaves the last alias in
place.  Neither const-optree.t nor lvref.t reads the variable after the loop
(checked s396), so the cheap correct move may be save-and-restore spelled in
the same rewrite (prepend `my $__PCL_SV0 = \%::a;` before the `for`, append
the restore after the block's `}`), or an announced divergence per the s329
effect-only boundary.  Decide with a probe against live perl.

BAR: the six/seven shapes above probed against perl; op/const-optree.t re-run
and its snapshot row spliced; corpus-diff; gate; the guard rows go in
Pl/t/refaliasing-01.t next to the assignment ones.


DONE s396b.  _repair_alias_foreach in Pl/Parser2.pm, called from the document
pre-pass chain next to the other PPI repairs.  Seven shapes probed against perl
5.40.3, all identical.  op/const-optree.t TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 86 ok / 62 (the 62
are optree-INSPECTION rows -- B:: inlinability and :method attributes -- the
same class as re::optimization, not aliasing).  Guard rows in
Pl/t/refaliasing-01.t incl. the INVERSE (an ordinary foreach over a list of
refs is untouched).

THE SEMANTIC QUESTION IS ANSWERED: perl does NOT restore an aliased PACKAGE
foreach variable (`our $s = q(orig); for \$::s (\q(a), \q(b)) {} print $s`
prints b), so no save/restore is needed and the naive rewrite IS perl.

ONE THING THE PROBES FOUND, pre-existing and NOT this task: a leading brace
group in a foreach list (`for my $r ({5,6},{7,8})`) is read as a LIST, not a
hash constructor -- recorded as the second population on task #286.
subject: refaliasing FOREACH: `for \my %e (@list)` - PPI cannot lex it (op/const-optree.t 148 rows)
